## Overview

With several pathogen strains the next-generation matrix often splits into blocks, one per
strain, because at the infection-free state no infected individual of one strain produces
infections of another. `R₀` is then the largest strain-specific reproduction number, and
the package returns a symbolic `max`. This holds even when the strains interact away from
the infection-free state, through cross-immunity or co-infection, because those
interactions are quadratic in the infected states and vanish on linearisation. This
vignette shows both cases, and a case where the block structure is broken (mutation
between strains).

## Two strains with partial cross-immunity

Recovered from strain 1 are protected from strain 2 by a factor `1 - σ₁₂`, and vice versa.

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters β₁ β₂ γ₁ γ₂ σ₁₂ σ₂₁ μ N
@variables S(t) I₁(t) I₂(t) R₁(t) R₂(t) J₁(t) J₂(t) R(t)
# Jᵢ: infected with strain i after recovering from the other strain
λ₁ = β₁ * (I₁ + J₁) / N
λ₂ = β₂ * (I₂ + J₂) / N
eqs = [D(S) ~ μ * N - (λ₁ + λ₂) * S - μ * S,
    D(I₁) ~ λ₁ * S - (γ₁ + μ) * I₁,
    D(I₂) ~ λ₂ * S - (γ₂ + μ) * I₂,
    D(R₁) ~ γ₁ * I₁ - σ₂₁ * λ₂ * R₁ - μ * R₁,
    D(R₂) ~ γ₂ * I₂ - σ₁₂ * λ₁ * R₂ - μ * R₂,
    D(J₁) ~ σ₁₂ * λ₁ * R₂ - (γ₁ + μ) * J₁,
    D(J₂) ~ σ₂₁ * λ₂ * R₁ - (γ₂ + μ) * J₂,
    D(R) ~ γ₁ * J₁ + γ₂ * J₂ - μ * R]
two = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :two_strain))
suggest_infected(two)
```

```{julia}
ngm = next_generation_matrix(two, [I₁, J₁, I₂, J₂])
irreducible_blocks(ngm.K)
```

At the infection-free state `R₁ = R₂ = 0`, so nobody is available for secondary infection
and the `J` states are not states-at-infection at all:

```{julia}
states_at_infection(ngm), ngm.K
```

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

The invasion of strain 2 into a population where strain 1 is endemic is a different
question, answered by linearising at strain 1's endemic equilibrium instead. The
`equilibrium` keyword accepts any state; here we leave `S`, `R₁` symbolic and read them
from an endemic equilibrium:

```{julia}
ngm_inv = next_generation_matrix(two, [I₂, J₂]; equilibrium = Dict(R₂ => 0, R => 0))
basic_reproduction_number(ngm_inv)
```

This is strain 2's *invasion reproduction number*: the susceptibles plus the partially
protected recovered from strain 1, weighted by the sojourn time of strain-2 infection.

## Mutation breaks the block structure

If strain 1 mutates into strain 2 during infection at rate `m`, an individual infected
with strain 1 can produce strain-2 infections, and the blocks merge into one irreducible
`2 × 2` matrix with a full closed form.

```{julia}
@parameters m
eqs_m = [D(S) ~ μ * N - (β₁ * I₁ + β₂ * I₂) * S / N - μ * S,
    D(I₁) ~ β₁ * I₁ * S / N - (γ₁ + μ + m) * I₁,
    D(I₂) ~ β₂ * I₂ * S / N + m * I₁ - (γ₂ + μ) * I₂,
    D(R) ~ γ₁ * I₁ + γ₂ * I₂ - μ * R]
mut = complete(System(eqs_m, t; name = :mutation))
ngm_m = next_generation_matrix(mut, [I₁, I₂])
ngm_m.K
```

`K[2, 1]` is the number of strain-2 infections caused by a strain-1 infected individual who
mutates before recovering. The matrix is triangular, so the spectrum is still the two
diagonal entries:

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ngm_m)
```

## Co-infection

Co-infection terms such as `I₁ I₂` do not affect `R₀` because they vanish at the
infection-free state:

```{julia}
@parameters κ
@variables C(t)
eqs_c = [D(S) ~ -(β₁ * I₁ + β₂ * I₂) * S / N,
    D(I₁) ~ β₁ * I₁ * S / N - γ₁ * I₁ - κ * I₁ * I₂,
    D(I₂) ~ β₂ * I₂ * S / N - γ₂ * I₂ - κ * I₁ * I₂,
    D(C) ~ 2κ * I₁ * I₂ - (γ₁ + γ₂) * C,
    D(R) ~ γ₁ * I₁ + γ₂ * I₂ + (γ₁ + γ₂) * C]
co = complete(System(eqs_c, t; name = :coinfection))
ngm_c = next_generation_matrix(co, [I₁, I₂, C]; equilibrium = Dict(S => N, R => 0))
states_at_infection(ngm_c), basic_reproduction_number(ngm_c)
```
